subject: Dedicated capacity options and minimum-GPU lifecycle for NebulaAI
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@nebulaai.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity options and minimum-GPU lifecycle for NebulaAI

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together three pragmatic reservation scenarios tailored to NebulaAI's initial traffic profile and the low-latency inference targets you mentioned. The attached workbook has the full math; below is a short summary so procurement and engineering can move faster.

High-level assumptions (see workbook tab "Assumptions"):
- Traffic: 1.2M inference calls/day initially, expected 30% month-over-month for Q1 if model adoption goes as planned.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation < 350ms (for the main text generation route).
- Model mix: 65% open LLM distil variants / 35% larger backbone for complex prompts.
- Typical sequence lengths: 128 tokens average.

Option 1 — Conservative (pilot):
- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared lanes),
- Minimum committed GPUs: 4 (soft floor),
- Ramp: 2→4 GPUs after month 1 if usage > 60% of pilot capacity, full 8 by month 3.
- Use case: validate integration, low cost.

Option 2 — Balanced (recommended for production proof):
- Cluster: 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs,
- Minimum committed GPUs: 12 (firm),
- Ramp: 12 initial, 18 at month 2 trigger, 24 by month 4.
- Buffer: 20% burst pool for short spikes.

Option 3 — Performance-first (scale):
- Cluster: 48 x A100-equivalent GPUs,
- Minimum committed GPUs: 32 (firm),
- Ramp: 32 initial with aggressive warm-start and autoscale to 48 under sustained traffic.

Notes on warm-start and cost levers: prefix caching and batch-size tuning will materially reduce effective GPU need for chat-heavy workloads; we can bake those into the onboarding playbook.

Attachments: nebulaai_reservation_options_v1.pdf, capacity_workbook_initial.xlsx

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm preferred option (1/2/3) and minimum committed GPUs, 2) we coordinate a short call with Grace to review warm-start and latency tuning, and 3) Karthik to finalize an onboarding-runbook and a SOW sketch for procurement.

Happy to walk through the workbook on a quick call — what does your schedule look like this week?

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

3) Procurement asked whether burst capacity is billed as consumed (true pay-as-you-go) or reserved credits (preferred).

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@nebulaai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-24T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and minimum-GPU lifecycle for NebulaAI

Olivia — great questions. Quick answers inline, then a short note on next steps.

1) Minimum-committed 12 GPUs in Option 2 is per-account and can be scoped by region. For your cross-region requirement we typically do a 75/25 primary/secondary split (example: 9 GPUs us-west / 3 GPUs us-east) — the workbook includes a regional tab with cost modeling. If you want strict per-region firm minimums we can update the commercial to reflect 12 firm per region.

2) p95 latency guarantee: At the 12-GPU floor we can guarantee p95 < 350ms for the baseline distil model under the traffic profile outlined in the workbook (that is, median sequence length ~128, no sustained 10x spikes). If you run the larger backbone simultaneously at sustained levels, the p95 will drift — we captured that in the SLA appendix draft (Drive link below). Degradation profile: +80–150ms p95 when large-model mix exceeds 30% sustained; automated fallback to a lower-cost variant reduces tail but may change output characteristics.

3) Burst billing: flexible — options are either "consumed burst" (pay-as-you-go) or pre-purchased burst credits with a discounted rate. Procurement preference for pre-purchased credits makes sense for forecasting; I'll include both line-items in the cost table.

I attached an updated workbook with a regional split and a short SLO appendix. Grace will own the technical onboarding and warm-start plan; Karthik will draft an initial SOW and an invoice cadence proposal.

Attachments: capacity_workbook_updated.xlsx
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nebula-capacity (SLA appendix & runbook draft)

Grace / Karthik — can you please review the workbook and SLO appendix and share a 1-page SOW + a cost table (firm floor vs burst credits) by EOD Wednesday? Olivia — if you have a preferred contract template, share the procurement contact and we'll align.

Thanks —
Ben
